text:
maya: Customer acme-prod reporting a spike of 502s after traffic shifted to eu-west. They say their client saw high latency and errors. Heartbeat shows us-west marked DOWN around 11:02 but our active probes were green on the ground. Ticket INC-4321 opened. Any ideas?

jon: @oncall tagging — looking at routing metrics now. Control plane chose eu-west via 'latency' policy. Health aggregator shows 3 missed heartbeats for us-west at ~11:02. Could be TTL mismatch or probe source IP churn. :thinking: 

sre-bot: healthcheck-alert: proxy-heartbeat-monitor detected 3 consecutive missed pings -> region us-west marked UNHEALTHY -> initiated failover to eu-west (auto-failover policy).

kevin: Can we fetch raw probe logs from the probe fleet and the aggregator logs? Also check if probe auth tokens rotated around 10:58 (secrets rotation window).

maya: Pasting a minimal repro from customer curl: 

```
curl -i https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-XXX" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
HTTP/2 502
server: nginx
x-region: eu-west
x-request-id: r-123
```

jon: Note the x-region header is eu-west already — client got routed there. That suggests the control plane changed routing earlier. I ran a quick config check: 

```
rctl get health-config acme-prod --region us-west
# ttl: 30s
# aggregator-ttl: 25s
```

jon: TTL mismatch looks likely — aggregator expects 25s but probes are set to 30s so it can see a heartbeat as missed if timing aligns poorly. Also saw a small burst of NAT IP rotation logs from probe pool at 11:01.

kevin: Confirmed aggregator config had stale value (25s). A rollout last night updated probe TTL to 30s but failed to update aggregator. I'm going to roll aggregator to 30s and temporarily disable auto-failover for acme-prod while we validate.

maya: I updated the support ticket with the current hypothesis and told the customer we're investigating. If we disable auto-failover, what are the risks for them?

jon: If we disable auto-failover, traffic stays pinned to current region. If the region actually goes offline, requests may error until we manually fail over. But it avoids oscillations and routing flaps caused by false negatives. We'll set a cooldown 120s before re-enabling.

sre-bot: action: disable-auto-failover acme-prod by kevin at 11:22 UTC; action-id a-987

kevin: Patching aggregator config to ttl=30s -> sync complete. Running synthetic checks (1000 requests) against us-west and eu-west to measure stability before re-enable.

maya: Customer just messaged: "errors dropped after 2 mins, seems back to normal" — they see most traffic to us-west again. I'll keep ticket open until re-enable.

jon: I'll own the postmortem. Initial follow-ups: 1) audit probe auth/token rotation timing, 2) CI check that validates TTL drift between probe and aggregator configs, 3) runbook update for disable-auto-failover steps and cooldown. Assigning to eng-sre + eng-platform.

kevin: Re-enable scheduled once synthetic checks pass and cooldown observed. Will post timeline in the ticket.

maya: Thanks everyone, I'll coordinate customer comms and close after re-enable.

(End of thread)
